examples.en: The whole audience stood up and applauded.
When the anthem played, the attendees stood up.
At the opening ceremony, everyone stood and observed a moment of silence.
When the judge enters, the spectators must stand.
When the show ended, people stood up and cheered.

examples.ko: 다리가 불편하신 분은 기립하지 않으셔도 돼요.
examples.en: Those with difficulty standing don't have to rise.

explain: 일상에서는 '일어서다'라고 해요. '기립하다'는 행사, 공연, 재판처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 쓰고, '기립 박수', '기립 투표', '기립 묵념'처럼 합쳐 쓰는 일이 많아요.

phrases.example: 공연이 끝나자 관객들이 기립 박수를 보냈어요.
phrases.en: When the performance ended, the audience gave a standing ovation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 많이 쓰는 짝말로, 일어서서 치는 박수를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common pairing and means applause given while standing.

phrases.en: When the song began, everyone stood up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기립하다'와 같은 뜻을 일상에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the everyday way to say the same thing as 기립하다.

phrases.en: The host said, 'Everyone, please rise.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사에서 사람들에게 일어나 달라고 정중히 부탁할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a polite request at an event for people to stand up.

explain_en: In daily life people say '일어서다'. '기립하다' is used in formal settings like ceremonies, performances, and courts, and often appears in compounds such as '기립 박수', '기립 투표', and '기립 묵념'.

examples.ko: 선수가 기합을 넣고 공을 힘껏 찼어요.
examples.en: The player let out a shout and kicked the ball with all his might.

examples.ko: 도장에서 큰 기합 소리가 울려 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: A loud shout echoed through the training hall.
I answered in a voice full of energy and spirit.
The baby burst into tears, startled by the shout.
He threw his opponent with a shout.
I heard there was a time when people were punished with hard physical drills.

explain: 운동이나 무술에서 힘을 모으려고 내는 소리를 말하고, '기합을 넣다'처럼 정신을 바짝 차리게 하는 말로도 써요. '기합을 받다'는 벌로 힘든 동작을 하는 것을 말해요.

phrases.en: I psyched myself up before entering the exam room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정신을 바짝 차리고 힘을 낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you focus your mind and gather your energy.

phrases.en: I was late for training, so I was disciplined by a senior.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌로 힘든 동작을 하게 되는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means being made to do tough exercises as punishment.

phrases.en: I heard a loud shout from the gym.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무술이나 운동에서 힘을 모으려고 지르는 소리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the shout made to focus strength in martial arts or sports.

explain_en: It is the shout made to gather strength in sports or martial arts, and '기합을 넣다' also means to get your spirit sharp and focused. '기합을 받다' means to be made to do hard physical drills as punishment.

examples.ko: 갑자기 공이 날아와서 반사적으로 고개를 숙였어요.
examples.en: A ball suddenly flew at me, and I ducked by reflex.
When I'm startled, I scream first, without thinking.
I answered 'I'm fine' automatically to that question.

examples.ko: 반사적인 행동이라서 저도 왜 그랬는지 몰라요.
examples.en: It was a reflex action, so I don't know why I did it either.
That's a reflexive reaction, so it's hard to change.
I laughed instinctively at the funny remark.

explain: 실제로는 '반사적으로', '반사적인 행동/반응'처럼 뒤에 붙여서 많이 써요. 생각할 틈 없이 몸이나 말이 먼저 나가는 상황에 쓰고, '무의식적으로'와 비슷해요. 좋고 나쁜 뜻은 없고 상황 설명에 써요.

phrases.en: When a car came, I stepped back by reflex.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각하기 전에 몸이 먼저 움직일 때 가장 자주 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, used when the body moves before you think.

phrases.en: I was suddenly startled and had a reflexive reaction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 활용형으로, 자동으로 나오는 반응을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form before a noun, describing an automatic reaction.

phrases.en: When my name was called, I answered automatically.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말도 생각 없이 먼저 나오는 상황에 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be used when words come out automatically without thought.

explain_en: In practice it appears as '반사적으로' or '반사적인 행동/반응'. It describes the body or mouth acting before you can think, and is close to '무의식적으로' (unconsciously). It is neutral and just describes the situation.

examples.ko: 발표 때 긴장해서 말이 자꾸 버벅댔어요.
examples.en: I got nervous during the presentation and kept stumbling over my words.
My computer is old, so programs keep lagging.
I felt frustrated because I kept stumbling when trying to speak English.
I practiced beforehand so I wouldn't stumble in the interview.
The game was lagging, so I couldn't win.

examples.ko: 처음 하는 일이라 좀 버벅대도 괜찮아요.
examples.en: It's your first time doing this, so it's fine if you fumble a bit.

explain: 말이나 동작이 매끄럽지 않고 자꾸 막힐 때 쓰는 구어체예요. 요즘은 컴퓨터나 게임이 끊기고 느려질 때도 많이 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '버벅거리다'도 써요.

phrases.en: I was nervous in the interview and kept stumbling over my words.
phrases.nuance_ko: '버벅대다'와 같은 뜻이고, 둘 다 구어체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 버벅대다; both are colloquial.

phrases.en: Don't stumble; try speaking slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이 막히는 사람에게 편하게 조언할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to advise someone who keeps getting stuck.

phrases.en: I keep stumbling when I speak English.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외국어나 발표처럼 말이 잘 안 나올 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for foreign languages or presentations when words won't come out.

explain_en: This is a colloquial word for when speech or movement keeps getting stuck and isn't smooth. These days it is also used when a computer or game lags. '버벅거리다' means the same.

examples.en: The teacher banged on the desk and spoke with fiery passion.

examples.ko: 그의 열변에 사람들이 모두 귀를 기울였어요.
examples.en: Everyone listened closely to his passionate speech.
When the fiery speech ended, applause broke out.
I even spoke with all my passion, but nobody was persuaded.

examples.ko: 그 연설가의 열변은 지금도 기억에 남아요.
examples.en: That speaker's fiery speech still stays in my memory.
He moved people's hearts with his passionate speech.

explain: 거의 '열변을 토하다'의 모양으로 써요. 그냥 '열심히 말하다'보다 목소리와 몸짓에 힘이 들어간 강한 말하기를 나타내요. 연설, 토론, 강의 같은 상황에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.example: 그는 환경 보호의 중요성에 대해 열변을 토했어요.
phrases.en: He spoke passionately about the importance of protecting the environment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '토하다'가 말을 쏟아낸다는 뜻으로 쓰여요. 열정을 담아 길고 힘 있게 주장하는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Here '토하다' means pouring words out. It describes arguing at length and with force and passion.

explain_en: It is almost always used in the form '열변을 토하다'. It is stronger than simply speaking hard, since voice and gestures are full of force. It fits speeches, debates and lectures.

en: to hum; to make a noise; to be noisy

examples.ko: 교실 밖에서 아이들이 웅성대는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear the children buzzing outside the classroom.

examples.ko: 발표 결과가 나오자 사람들이 웅성대기 시작했어요.
examples.en: When the results were announced, people began to murmur.
The lights suddenly went out, and the audience started murmuring.
People are gathered in the lobby, buzzing with talk.
Please stop the chatter and sit quietly.

examples.ko: 무슨 일인지 복도가 웅성대서 나가 봤어요.
examples.en: The hallway was buzzing, so I went out to see what was going on.

explain: 여러 사람이 낮은 목소리로 한꺼번에 말해서 어수선하게 들리는 소리예요. 크게 떠드는 '시끄럽다'와 달리, 무슨 말인지 모르게 섞여 들리는 느낌이에요. '웅성거리다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: Students are murmuring in the hallway.
phrases.nuance_ko: '웅성대다'와 같은 뜻이고 더 자주 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '웅성대다' and a more common form.

phrases.en: People are gathered, murmuring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 계속 이어지는 느낌을 부사로 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb conveys a continuing murmur of voices.

phrases.en: I saw people murmuring at the entrance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

explain_en: It describes many people talking in low voices at once, creating a confused hum. Unlike loud chatter ('시끄럽다'), the words blend together so you cannot make them out. It can be swapped with '웅성거리다' with almost the same meaning.

examples.en: This song was made on the spot.
The improvised performance was really cool.
I went on a spur-of-the-moment trip with friends.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 즉흥 연기를 아주 잘해요.
examples.en: That actor is very good at improvised acting.
I gave the presentation off the cuff, so I was really nervous.
Spur-of-the-moment decisions are sometimes regretted.

explain: 즉흥은 미리 준비하지 않고 그 자리에서 바로 하는 거예요. '즉흥 연주', '즉흥 여행'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙이거나 '즉흥적이다'로 많이 써요. '계획 없이 갑자기'라는 가볍고 재미있는 느낌이 있을 때가 많아요.

phrases.en: I went to the sea on impulse over the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '즉흥'은 명사이고, '즉흥적으로'는 계획 없이 바로 행동하는 방식을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '즉흥' is a noun; '즉흥적으로' describes how you act, on the spur of the moment without a plan.
phrases.en_equiv: on the spur of the moment

phrases.en: I heard a great improvised performance on the street.
phrases.nuance_ko: '즉흥'을 다른 명사 앞에 붙인 가장 흔한 짝말이에요. 악보 없이 그 자리에서 연주한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, with '즉흥' placed before another noun; it means playing on the spot without a score.

phrases.en: I set off on a spontaneous trip with a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 계획하지 않고 갑자기 떠나는 가볍고 재미있는 여행을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a light, fun trip taken suddenly without advance planning.

explain_en: 즉흥 means doing something on the spot, with no preparation. It usually sits before another noun, as in 즉흥 연주, or becomes 즉흥적이다. It often has a light, fun feel of acting without a plan.

en: all one's strength; one's whole heart

examples.ko: 선수들은 마지막 경기에 혼신의 힘을 다했어요.
examples.en: The players gave everything they had in the last game.
He put his whole heart into preparing for the exam.
After an all-out effort, I finally passed.

examples.ko: 가수가 혼신의 열창으로 마지막 노래를 불렀어요.
examples.en: The singer sang the last song with all her heart.
My parents poured everything into growing their shop.

examples.ko: 혼신을 다한 연기에 관객들이 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: The audience applauded the all-out performance.

explain: 거의 '혼신의 힘/노력/연기'나 '혼신을 다하다'의 모양으로만 써요. '최선을 다하다'보다 몸과 마음을 전부 쏟는 느낌이 강해서 공연, 경기, 큰 시험 이야기에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.example: 마라톤 선수가 혼신의 힘을 다해 달렸어요.
phrases.en: The marathon runner ran with all his strength.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸과 마음의 힘을 전부 쏟는다는 뜻으로 가장 많이 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, meaning pouring out all body and mind strength.

phrases.example: 배우의 혼신의 연기에 관객이 박수를 쳤어요.
phrases.en: The audience applauded the actor's all-out performance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연기나 공연에 모든 것을 쏟았을 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits an acting or stage performance where one gave everything.

phrases.en: She sang with all her heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: '혼신을 다하다'를 이어서 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The connecting form of 혼신을 다하다.

explain_en: It is used almost only in set patterns such as '혼신의 힘/노력/연기' and '혼신을 다하다'. It feels stronger than '최선을 다하다', as if you pour your whole body and mind into it, and suits talk of performances, matches and big exams.

examples.ko: 오늘 뉴스에서 우리 대표팀의 활약상을 자세히 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: Today's news showed our national team's performance in detail.

examples.ko: 그 선수의 활약상이 요즘 인터넷에서 화제예요.
examples.en: That player's performance is a hot topic online these days.

examples.ko: 신입 사원의 활약상은 회의 때마다 칭찬을 받았어요.
examples.en: The new employee's great work was praised at every meeting.
My friends applauded my older brother's brilliant performance.

examples.ko: 활약상 소개 영상을 보면서 저도 힘이 났어요.
examples.en: Watching the video introducing their achievements gave me energy too.

examples.ko: 지난 대회에서 보인 활약상 덕분에 그 선수는 유명해졌어요.
examples.en: Thanks to his performance in the last tournament, that player became famous.

explain: '~의 활약상'처럼 앞에 사람이나 팀을 붙여서 써요. 뉴스, 스포츠 기사, 소개글에서 '활약상을 전하다/소개하다'와 함께 잘 나와요. 친구와 이야기할 때는 '진짜 잘했어', '대단했어'처럼 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 이번 경기에서 큰 활약을 했어요.
phrases.en: That player made a big contribution in this game.
phrases.nuance_ko: '활약상'에서 '상'을 뺀 말로, 더 넓게 쓰고 '활약하다'로도 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Drops the '상' from 활약상; broader in use and also works as the verb 활약하다.

phrases.en: A reporter covered our team's performance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 기사에서 누군가의 활동 모습을 알린다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in news to mean reporting on someone's performance.

phrases.example: 신인 선수가 첫 경기에서 맹활약을 펼쳤어요.
phrases.en: The rookie player gave a brilliant performance in his first game.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맹'이 붙어서 아주 눈에 띄게 잘한 활약을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The prefix 맹 stresses an especially striking, excellent performance.

explain_en: It is used after a person or team, as in '~의 활약상'. It goes with verbs like '전하다' and '소개하다' in news, sports articles and profiles. In casual talk people usually say things like '진짜 잘했어' or '대단했어' instead.
